summary.title: Interfaces › Cheat Sheet
summary.one_liner: A checklist of opinionated UI, animation, typography, color, accessibility, layout and microcopy rules for building better interfaces.
keywords: smart punctuation curly quotes em dash
takeaways: Nest border radius concentrically (outer = inner + padding) and prefer optical over geometric alignment.
Animate from the trigger, keep exits subtler than entrances, and name transition properties instead of using transition: all.
Use .woff2 fonts, tabular-nums for changing numbers, and keep long-form text to 60–75 characters per line.
Build semantic color tokens by purpose, and create a separate dark mode palette rather than inverting the light one.
Use native HTML elements, visible focus styles, 24–44px hit areas, aria-invalid on errors, and respect reduced motion.
summary.summary: This is a personal opinionated cheat sheet from interfaces.dev, mixing best practices with the author's preferences. It is organized into sections covering user interface details, animation, typography, colors, accessibility, layout and writing. Each rule is stated briefly, often with concrete values (such as scale 0.95–0.98, 200ms transitions, 60–75 character line lengths, or 44x44px touch targets) and sometimes with recommended vs. not recommended examples. It is a quick reference rather than a tutorial, so the code snippets are short CSS and HTML properties.
